title: Addition and Subtraction Word Problems within 20
standard_text: 1.3B use objects and pictorial models to solve word problems involving joining, separating, and comparing sets within 20 and unknowns as any one of the terms in the problem; 1.3F generate and solve problem situations when given a number sentence involving addition or subtraction of numbers within 20; 1.5D represent word problems involving addition and subtraction of whole numbers up to 20 using concrete and pictorial models and number sentences
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 word problem worksheets for Texas TEKS 1.3B, 1.3F and 1.5D: join, separate, compare and missing number stories within 20. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Join: add. Take away or compare: subtract.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Read the story. Is something joined, taken away, or compared?
  • Join: add. Take away: subtract. How many more: subtract.
  • Write a number sentence with a box for the unknown: 7 + ☐ = 12.
  • Check: does the answer make sense in the story?

Examples

Example

Ava has 7 shells. She finds some more. Now she has 12.

7 + ☐ = 12

Answer: 5 shells

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding when the story takes awayLook for words like gave away or ate.
Adding in a compare storyHow many more means subtract.
Answering with a number from the storyFind the unknown.

items.q: Carlos made a tower with 7 blocks. He took off 4 blocks. How many blocks are in the tower now?
items.e: Start with 7. Take away 4: 7 − 4 = 3. Answer: 3 blocks.

items.q: Liam has 7 blocks. Sofia has 3 blocks. How many more blocks does Liam have than Sofia?
items.e: Match them up. Liam has 4 extra. Find the difference: 7 − 3 = 4. Do not add. Check: 3 + 4 = 7. Answer: 4 blocks.
